newsitem.title: UK: Brady bonds quiet in London despite Mexico, Russia.
newsitem.headline: Brady bonds quiet in London despite Mexico, Russia.

text.p: Brady bond market activity was subdued in Europe despite Mexico's jumbo refinancing and amid talk Russia's latest Eurobond may be larger than the $1.0 billion being touted, dealers said on Wednesday.
"Obviously the Mexico deal is good news. Retiring the old debt for cheaper paper was the right decision but it hasn't encouraged any activity," a German bank trader here said.

Mexico said on Tuesday it will call the $6.0 billion FRN due 2001 it launched last July, refinancing with the proceeds of bonds launched earlier this year plus a fresh $2.0 billion from three new deals.
Elsewhere, there was talk Russia's latest Eurobond, a 10-year deal due Thursday via J.P. Morgan and SBC Warburg, would be much larger than the expected $1.0 billion.
One banker said the size could easily be $1.5 billion, while another said $2.0 was a possibility. "the demand is there, said
Whatever the size, dealers were agreed on 375 basis points as the probable launch spread.
Russia, which last Friday reaffirmed it would raise up to $3.5 billion internationally in 1997, raised $1.2 billion in March via a mark bond and has plans for a global dollar bond in the autumn.
At 0940 GMT Russian VN US$ was bid at 91.125, down 0.375 point on the day.
